# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("LiricRajlic_2024_mRNA6231"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("LiricRajlic_2024_mRNA6231"))$description`
* Article: [CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol. 2024;13(6):1067-1076](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13142)

mRNA-6231 is a lipid-nanoparticle-encapsulated mRNA encoding a human
interleukin-2 mutein fused to human serum albumin (HSA-IL2m), developed to
selectively expand regulatory T cells (Tregs). Because the systemic lipid and
mRNA concentrations are below assay quantitation, no drug concentration is
fitted; the model is a *kinetic-pharmacodynamic* (dose-driven) cascade from a
subcutaneous depot, through a virtual mRNA transit compartment, to saturable
synthesis of HSA-IL2m protein, an effect compartment, and an indirect-response
turnover model for the percentage of FOXP3+ Tregs.

# Population

The model was fitted to data from three non-GLP studies in male cynomolgus
monkeys (Methods, "Study design"). Study 1 (N = 16, aged 2-4 years) gave
repeat subcutaneous doses of 1, 3, 6 or 10 ug/kg on Days 1, 15 and 29. Study 2
(N = 12, aged 2-4 years) gave single doses of 3 or 10 ug/kg or a flat 10 ug
total dose. Study 3 (N = 16, aged 2-5 years, naive and non-naive) gave single
doses of 10 or 30 ug/kg or a flat 100 ug total dose. HSA-IL2m protein was
measured in plasma by ELISA and percentage Tregs (FOXP3+ of CD4+) in
cryopreserved PBMCs by flow cytometry. The allometric reference body weight is
2.5 kg.

The same information is available programmatically via the model's `population`
metadata (`readModelDb("LiricRajlic_2024_mRNA6231")()$population`).

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/LiricRajlic_2024_mRNA6231.R`. The table
below collects them in one place for review.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `d/dt(depot)` (SC absorption) | n/a | Table 2, equation 1 |
| `d/dt(transit1)` (virtual mRNA transit) | n/a | Table 2, equation 2 |
| `d/dt(central)` (saturable HSA-IL2m synthesis + elimination) | n/a | Table 2, equation 3 |
| `d/dt(effect)` (effect-compartment equilibration) | n/a | Table 2, equation 4 |
| `d/dt(treg)` (indirect-response Treg turnover) | n/a | Table 2, equation 5 |
| `treg(0) = kin/kout` | n/a | Table 2, equation 6 |
| Allometric scaling of ka, CLt, Vt, V, CLIL2, IL2kp | exponents -0.25, 0.65, 1, 1, 0.85, -0.25 | Table 2, equations 7-11 |
| `lka` (ka) | 0.0749 1/h | Table 3 |
| `lcl_transit` (CLt) | 12.865 mL/h | Table 3 |
| `lvt` (Vt, fixed) | 1.0 mL | Table 3 |
| `lvc` (V) | 171.56 mL | Table 3 |
| `lksyn` (IL2kp) | 4570.3 | Table 3 |
| `lkm_syn` (IL2k50) | 0.1312 ug/mL | Table 3 |
| `lcl` (CLIL2) | 1.529 mL/h | Table 3 |
| `lke0` (ke0) | 0.011 1/h | Table 3 |
| `lkin` (kin-Treg) | 0.0597 %/h | Table 3 |
| `lkout` (kout-Treg) | 0.0152 1/h | Table 3 |
| `lemax` (Emax) | 2.84 | Table 3 |
| `lhill` (gam) | 2.47 | Table 3 |
| `lec50` (EC50) | 5.08 ng/mL | Table 3 |
| IIV on IL2kp, CLIL2, kin-Treg, Emax | 51.3, 22.8, 36.5, 30.2 %CV | Table 3 |
| Proportional residual error (IL-2, Treg) | 43.4, 27.1 %CV | Table 3 |

# Virtual cohort

Original observed data are not publicly available. The figures below use a
virtual population of male cynomolgus monkeys at the 2.5 kg allometric
reference body weight, reproducing the Study 1 multiple-dose design (doses on
Days 1, 15 and 29). Between-subject variability comes from the four model IIV
terms (on IL2kp, CLIL2, kin-Treg and Emax).

Because this is a two-endpoint model (HSA-IL2m `Cc` and `treg`), observation
rows name the observable (`cmt = "Cc"` / `cmt = "treg"`) rather than the backing
ODE state, as rxode2 requires for multi-endpoint models.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(6231)

doses <- tibble::tibble(
  dose_lbl = factor(c("1 ug/kg", "3 ug/kg", "6 ug/kg", "10 ug/kg"),
                    levels = c("1 ug/kg", "3 ug/kg", "6 ug/kg", "10 ug/kg")),
  dose_ugkg = c(1, 3, 6, 10)
)
n_per <- 100L               # <= 200 per arm
wt_ref <- 2.5               # kg, allometric reference (individual weights not reported)
dose_days <- c(0, 14, 28)   # Days 1, 15, 29 relative to first dose
obs_h <- seq(0, 72 * 24, by = 12)

# Build event rows without tidyr::crossing() on a data frame that carries a
# factor column -- crossing() would expand the factor to all its levels and
# silently duplicate subjects. expand_grid() on plain id/time vectors, then a
# join of per-subject covariates by id, is safe.
make_cohort <- function(dl, dmgk, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n_per)
  amt_ug <- dmgk * wt_ref
  dose_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_days * 24) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, amt = amt_ug, cmt = "depot")
  pk_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_h) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "Cc")
  pd_rows <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_h) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "treg")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, pk_rows, pd_rows) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = wt_ref, dose_lbl = dl) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, WT, dose_lbl) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(doses)), function(i) {
  make_cohort(doses$dose_lbl[i], doses$dose_ugkg[i], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("LiricRajlic_2024_mRNA6231")
# Structural + between-subject variability (IPRED); residual error is left off
# so the bands below are a model-prediction VPC. useLinCmt = FALSE because the
# synthesis cascade is not a linear-compartment model.
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events,
  sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
  keep = c("dose_lbl"), returnType = "data.frame")
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-2a}
# Replicates Figure 2a of Liric Rajlic 2024: multiple-dose HSA-IL2m in plasma.
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), Cc > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_lbl, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50, colour = dose_lbl, fill = dose_lbl)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "HSA-IL2m (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose", fill = "Dose",
       title = "Figure 2a - multiple-dose HSA-IL2m",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 2a of Liric Rajlic 2024 (Days 1, 15, 29).")
```

```{r figure-2b}
# Replicates Figure 2b of Liric Rajlic 2024: multiple-dose percentage Tregs.
sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(treg)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_lbl, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(treg, 0.05), Q50 = quantile(treg, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(treg, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50, colour = dose_lbl, fill = dose_lbl)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "FOXP3+ of CD4+ T cells (%)", colour = "Dose", fill = "Dose",
       title = "Figure 2b - multiple-dose percentage Tregs",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 2b of Liric Rajlic 2024 (Days 1, 15, 29).")
```

# PKNCA validation

HSA-IL2m protein has a well-defined post-dose peak, so Cmax and Tmax over the
first dosing interval (Days 1-14, before the Day-15 dose) are compared against
the NCA values the paper reports for Study 1, Day 1 (Table 1). AUC and
half-life are not compared: HSA-IL2m is synthesized rather than dosed, so an
exposure integral and a terminal slope are not the quantities the paper
tabulates.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time <= 14 * 24) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, dose_lbl)

# Guarantee a time = 0 row per subject (pre-dose HSA-IL2m is 0).
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, dose_lbl) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, dose_lbl, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, dose_lbl, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | dose_lbl + id)

dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time == 0) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dose_lbl)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | dose_lbl + id)

intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 14 * 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

```{r nca_compare}
# Study 1, Day 1 NCA (Table 1): Emax (= Cmax) in ng/mL, tmax median in days.
# tmax converted to hours to match the PKNCA output unit.
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~dose_lbl,  ~cmax, ~tmax,
  "1 ug/kg",   26.7, 3.0 * 24,
  "3 ug/kg",   84.9, 3.0 * 24,
  "6 ug/kg",  127.0, 3.0 * 24,
  "10 ug/kg", 248.0, 3.0 * 24
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "dose_lbl",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", tmax = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 30
)

cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose" = dose_lbl) |>
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Simulated vs. published Study 1 Day-1 NCA. * differs from reference by >30%.",
    align = c("l", "l", "r", "r")
  )
```

```{r nca_gate}
# Median simulated Cmax per dose group against the Table 1 Day-1 Emax. A
# mis-transcribed synthesis rate, clearance, volume or dose unit moves Cmax by
# well over a factor of two, so a 25% band on the group median is a
# structural check and is insensitive to which subjects land in the tails
# (each median is over 100 subjects; the rendered differences are within 17%).
cmax_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax") |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_lbl) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose_lbl = as.character(dose_lbl)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published, by = "dose_lbl") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (sim - cmax) / cmax)
stopifnot(nrow(cmax_chk) == 4L, all(abs(cmax_chk$pct) < 25))
```

The simulated median Cmax is within 20% of the published Day-1 Emax at all
four dose levels. One discrepancy is visible and is *not* tuned away:

- **Tmax is earlier than the NCA median.** The typical-value model peaks at
  about 1.5 days (36 h on the 12-hour simulation grid), whereas the Table 1
  median Tmax for Study 1 is 3 days. The densely sampled single-dose Study 3
  shows the opposite (median Tmax 0.7-0.9 days), so the single structural model
  sits between studies whose apparent absorption and synthesis kinetics
  differ. The NCA Tmax also depends on the sparse, uneven sampling schedule.

The maintainers also simulated the Study 3 single doses (10 and 30 ug/kg, and a
flat 100 ug) at the typical values. The flat 100 ug dose reproduces the
observed Emax (431 vs 432 ng/mL), but the model over-predicts the 10 and 30
ug/kg Emax (about 195 and 376 vs 133 and 177 ng/mL). This dose-dependent
mismatch is what the dose effect on CLIL2 in Table 2, equation 8 would absorb;
that term cannot be included here (see Assumptions and deviations).

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Dose effect on CLIL2 omitted.** Table 2, equation 8 scales CLIL2 by
  `(Dose/0.0045)^nonlin`, but the value of the `nonlin` exponent is not reported
  anywhere in the paper (it is absent from Table 3, the text, the figures and
  the supplement). The maintainers omit the term (equivalent to `nonlin = 0`,
  i.e. the factor is 1). With the term at unity the model reproduces the
  low-dose Study 1 HSA-IL2m Emax of Table 1; the residual over-/under-prediction
  of Cmax at the extreme single doses is the part of the dose nonlinearity this
  omitted term would have absorbed.
- **Allometric scaling retained with a 2.5 kg reference.** The monkey fit
  (Table 3) is reported at the 2.5 kg reference individual. Equations 7-11 build
  in body-weight scaling with fixed exponents; the maintainers keep this scaling
  so the model can be forward-projected to other body weights, as the authors
  did when extrapolating to humans.
- **Treg dose-response is flatter than the observed data.** With the published
  EC50 of 5.08 ng/mL, effect-site HSA-IL2m exceeds EC50 even at 1 ug/kg, so
  the typical-value Treg peak saturates near the model ceiling
  `(1 + Emax) * kin/kout` (about 15%) at every Study 1 dose (about 13.5% at
  1 ug/kg, 14.8% at 10 ug/kg). Figure 2b shows dose-graded mean peaks from
  about 5% to about 30%. The Table 3 estimates are encoded exactly as
  printed; Figure 2b is reproduced only qualitatively, and no Treg value is
  asserted.
- **Human extrapolation not reproduced here.** The paper's human prediction at a
  70 ug dose (median peak HSA-IL2m 86.4 ng/mL, median peak Tregs 10.8%) is a
  downstream application of equations 7-11 at a 70 kg body weight. The maintainers
  were unable to reproduce that peak HSA-IL2m from Table 2 + Table 3 alone, which
  is consistent with the unreported `nonlin` term above materially affecting the
  low-dose (1 ug/kg equivalent) human projection. The shipped model is the
  monkey KPD model; the human projection is documented but not asserted.
- **Body weights fixed at 2.5 kg.** Per-animal body weights are not reported, so
  the virtual cohort uses the 2.5 kg allometric reference for every subject;
  between-subject spread comes only from the four model IIV terms.
- **IIV reported as %CV.** Table 3 reports interindividual variability as a
  percentage; the model encodes each as a log-normal variance via
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`.
- **Dose and concentration units differ by species.** The dose (and depot /
  transit states) are in ug of mRNA-6231, whereas the HSA-IL2m concentration is
  in ng/mL of a different molecular species synthesized downstream; the IL2kp
  synthesis coefficient carries the unit bridge, so no direct ug-to-ng dose
  conversion applies.
- **No correction notice** for this article was found as of 2026-10-30.
```
